verdicts.reason: The repo claim is true: E-7-Y is in no `next` list. A simulation with js-yaml and rules.js shows that once edges are added, E-7-Y's own age [18,24] and koreanEdu 1 gates filter readers correctly. The legal basis comes from a government briefing and the D-10 manual text, both fetched by an earlier verifier (d4#3/d4#2); I could not re-fetch them because this session had no network (search budget used up, WebFetch DNS errors). The fix names the wrong D-4 sub-code: D-4-1 is the language-institute student, while the Korea-schooled cohort holds D-4-3. It also leaves out D-10-1, whose needs already encode this youth track ({koreanEdu: 1, ageUnder: 25}); the briefing pairs D-10 and E-7-Y for the same cohort.

verdicts.reason: The repo claim is true: E-7-S1 and E-7-S2 lack F-2-T, while E-7-1, E-1, E-3, F-2-7 and E-7-T all have it. F-2-T has an in-Korea `change` list in visadocs that is not split by prior status, and the change rule covers D-7 to E-7 holders, so E-7-S qualifies. I could not re-fetch the manual quote (no network). It is consistent with the repo's own E-7-T→F-2-T note and with the 법무부고시 제2026-160호 summary in finding f2#6. The proposed note is a new untranslated sentence and only describes the 2×-GNI route, which does not matter for E-7-S1 (that status already needs 3× GNI). Also, with today's loose F-2-T `needs`, these edges would open F-2-T to anyone with 5 years' experience, so they must ship together with the F-2-T needs fix (e7-special#2).

verdicts.reason: The repo claim is true. A simulation shows that a high-school-only reader with 5 years' experience gets F-2-T as OPEN from E-7-1, E-7-T and D-10-T, because `[{edu:4,rank:3},{experience:5}]` means either one is enough. The base Top-Tier criteria are indeed degree AND career. But according to 고시 제2026-160호 as read by f2#6 and none-rest#0 (not re-fetched by me), an income of 4× GNI waives either the degree or the career condition. F-2-T also has a science-and-technology track (visadocs Ⅱ. 과학기술 분야), while E-7-T's needs come only from the industry track. The conjunctions are still the best gate the engine can express, since it has no income fact and PI-level science applicants are nearly always covered by {edu:5, rank:3, experience:5}. The 4× waiver should go in `how` so a blocked reader can see the exception.

verdicts.reason: The repo claim is true: E-7-T's next list has F-2-T, F-2-7, F-5-1, F-6-1, F-2-3, D-2-x and D-10-1, but no F-5-9, F-5-10, F-5-15 or F-5-11. E-7-S1 and E-7-S2 lack them too, while E-7-1, E-1 and E-3 have them. Decree 별표 1의3 defines these PR grounds by personal conditions with no prior-status restriction, which matches my own recollection of the decree text; the MOJ Visa Navigator (as quoted in f5#5) says they are open directly from 전문인력 (E-1 to E-7). All four targets have `change` lists in visadocs, and their own needs (F-5-9 {edu:5, stem}, F-5-10 {edu:3, stem} or {koreanEdu:4}, F-5-15 {koreanEdu:5}) keep the gating. I only adjusted the fix to add E-7-1's existing 4-language notes on every F-5-9/F-5-15 entry and to apply the same four entries to E-7-S1/E-7-S2, under the same decree logic.

verdicts.reason: The repo claim is true: E-7-S1, E-7-S2 and E-7-T are the only E-7 sub-codes without F-2-R, while E-7-1/2/3/4/4R and E-7-Y have it. The legal side rests only on inference. The visadocs F-2-R change case is generic ('lawful resident'), and the repo's own D-10-1→F-2-R note frames eligibility as an exclusion list (D-3, D-4, E-6-2, E-8, E-9, E-10, G-1, H-1) that does not name E-7-S or E-7-T. That suggests the claim is right and the bare-edge fix would be harmless, since `lang` never blocks and F-2-R has a change list. But neither the finding nor I could find a primary Korean text listing which prior statuses qualify, and this session had no network to fetch the 2026 chapter 37. Impact is low.
